title: Sunday school horns taken on the boat and replaced in Memphis
summary: They took band horns without permission, then spent their first pay in Memphis on two $20 horns and shipped the borrowed ones back to Mrs. Allen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And we were together. Now we don't have horns. But so what I did, I'll show you, when you're brought up right, what we done, we don't have any horns. We've got the Sunday school horns. They let you take them home, but not on the road, you know.

So now we've got the Sunday school horns and we take these horns and go on the boat with them, and our first payday, we had it all planned. Our first payday, we was in Memphis, so we got our $40.00, and we went out and bought two horns, $20.00 apiece. Wasn't nothing brand new, $20.00 apiece, and we bought them and had them to crate our horns up and send them back to the Sunday school. Sure. You never thought of, you know, keeping them, like kids do today. They'd forget all about it, you know. So it was on our minds all the time, we've got to get these horns back.
Yeah, because she didn't know you'd taken them.
But that must have been quite a thrill, to have bought your own horn.

Oh, yeah, we bought our own horns. Well, I think the main thing that made us do that was because we knew that we were doing wrong by taking them in the first place. We had to get them back as quick as possible.
Or else you'd never come back home, because your family's going to come down on you and --
Sure, if you steal the horns.
Stealing the horns and things, you know.
